desc.text: the monthly all-hands

situation.text: Optimising the onboarding funnel at LEO Innovation Lab, on the hypothesis that more notification opt-ins would raise activation.
situation.quote: At LEO Innovation Lab, we were optimising the onboarding funnel. We hypothesised that increasing notification opt-ins would increase activation.

task.text: Test a contextually-triggered opt-in shown at exactly the right moment.
task.quote: We got clever: a contextually-triggered opt-in shown at exactly the right moment.

action.text: The split test won on conversion but activation barely moved: the opt-in sat too late in the funnel. Rolled out a simpler opt-in early in the funnel, lifting net activation, and presented the mistake at the next company all-hands.
action.quote: We launched a split test, and the conversion rate was amazing... but activation barely moved. What happened? We'd placed the opt-in late in the funnel where very few users reached it. High conversion rate × tiny audience = marginal impact. We quickly rolled out a simpler opt-in early in the funnel. Lower conversion rate, but far more users saw it, so net activation was much higher. I presented this mistake at the next company all-hands.
